tech.name: An AI-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis, written in Lean and checked by machine
tech.released: announced 2026-11-20; certified by the Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative 2026-11-21
tech.status: Lean proof certified correct; human understanding and write-up still in progress
tech.one_line: Levent Alpöge, working with Claude, released a 17-million-line Lean proof of the Riemann hypothesis; machines checked every step within a day, though no human can read it yet.

predecessor.name: A proof checked by human experts reading it, which for a hard problem takes months or years

hook.text: I know the world moves fast. So you probably missed a huge AI breakthrough last week! On November 20th, a mathematician at Anthropic, working with Claude, released a proof of the Riemann hypothesis!

your_move.text: Ask what checks the AI's work: tests for code, sources for facts, a proof checker for math.

takeaway.text: When AI's work is too big to read, trust the checker. Subscribe and comment.
